question: All of the following are true of variable annuities, except:
choices: Funds from variable annuities are kept in accounts that are separate from the insurance company's general account
A variable annuity has two phases; accumulation and annuitization
Typically a customer makes contributions into a variable annuity with after-tax dollars
Variable annuities are not subject to regulations by both SEC and FINRA because they are only considered to be insurance products
explanation: Variable annuities are considered to be both an insurance product and a security and are subject to regulations by the SEC, FINRA, as well as by each state.

question: Which of following documents is NOT unique to margin accounts?
explanation:
A new account form must be completed whether an account is set up as a cash or a margin account.
The paperwork that is unique to opening margin accounts includes the margin agreement, which the customer must sign, pledging the securities in the account as collateral for the margin loan; the loan consent agreement, which is customarily signed, where the customer permits the securities in the account to be lent out for short sales by others; and the credit disclosure statement, which explains how the loan balance is computed and interest is charged.

question: To sell short a listed stock in a margin account requires a deposit of:
choices: 25% of the price of the transaction
50% of the price of the transaction
25% of the closing price of the security that day
50% of the closing price of the security that day
explanation: Regulation T requires that 50% of the sale amount, based on the price of the trade, be deposited to sell a stock short. The closing price has no effect on the deposit amount required.

question: Prior to opening an options account, all of the following steps must be taken EXCEPT:
choices: delivering the options disclosure document to the customer
receiving the signed options agreement from the customer
approving the first transaction in the account
explanation:
The customer has 15 days after the account is opened to sign and return the options agreement.
All of the other steps must be completed prior to opening the account - the new account form must be completed; the customer must be delivered an Options Disclosure Document (ODD); and the first transaction (as well as the account itself) must be approved in writing by the Registered Options Principal.

question: Any changes in value of a variable annuity accumulation unit are directly related to changes in the:
choices: Value of the securities funding the separate account
explanation: Since the separate account of investments funds a variable annuity, accumulation unit values are directly influenced by changes in the values of the securities in the separate account.

question: Which statement is TRUE about a minor in a custodial account under UGMA (Uniform Gifts To Minors Act) reaching legal age?
choices: The account must be transferred into the name of the new adult
The account is transferred into the name of the new adult when requested by the custodian
The account is transferred into the name of the new adult when requested by the parents
The account must be liquidated and the proceeds paid to the new adult
explanation: Under UGMA, when a minor in a custodial account reaches legal age, then the new adult simply presents proof of age, along with a government issued photo I.D. and the account is transferred into that person's name only.

question: Marilyn writes an ABC Aug 20 put @ 4. What is the maximum amount she could lose on this option?
explanation: Since Marilyn wrote a put, she is obligated to purchase 100 shares of the stockat the strike priceif the option is exercised. If ABC company drops to zero, she would lose$20 per share minus the premium. Her maximum loss would be($20- $4) x 100= $1,600.

question: A distribution from a Section 529 Plan would be subject to a 10% penalty tax if the beneficiary:
explanation: Payments from Section 529 Plans made to colleges, universities, vocational schools, and any other accredited post secondary education institution are not taxable. Distributions made to pay for "non-qualified" expenses are subject to regular income tax plus a 10% penalty tax (on the earnings in the account only). Refunds made because of death or disability of the beneficiary, or because the beneficiary received a scholarship, are not subject to the 10% penalty tax, but are still subject to regular income tax (on the earnings in the account only).

question: To prevent financial exploitation of seniors, FINRA requires that when opening an account for a client, reasonable efforts must be made to obtain the name, phone number, and mailing or e-mail address of a(n):
explanation:
To address growing problems with financial exploitation of vulnerable senior citizens, FINRA requires that "reasonable efforts" be made to obtain the name and contact information of a "trusted contact person" when an account is being opened. Note that this requirement applies to any new account, not just to accounts opened by senior citizens (age 65 or older).
If a member places a temporary hold on a senior citizen's account because of suspected financial exploitation, within 2 business days of placing the hold, all parties authorized to do business in the account must be notified, as well as the trusted contact person.
The "idea" is that the trusted contact person will take the steps necessary to stop the financial exploitation of the senior citizen (such as filing a complaint with the police).

topic: Accounts for Employees of Other Firms
question: When completing a new account form, you discover that the customer is an accounting supervisor at another FINRA member firm. Under FINRA rules, all of the following procedures are required EXCEPT:
choices: Prior to opening the account, written approval of the employing member must be obtained
The associated person opening the account must give written notice to the executing member of his or her association with the employer member
Duplicate confirmations and statements must be sent to the employer member on request
Annual account summaries of all activity must be sent to the employer member
explanation:
FINRA requires that if an employee of another FINRA member firm (whether registered or unregistered) wishes to open an account:
- prior written consent of the employing member firm must be obtained;
- the executing member must be notified in writing of the employee's association with another member firm; and
- on written request of the employer member, the executing member must provide duplicate confirmations and statements.

Note that the rule applies to "associated persons" of a member firm opening an account at another member - and an associated person is either an officer or a registered or unregistered employee of the member firm, with an exception given to anyone who only performs clerical or ministerial duties.
Not only does the rule apply to accounts opened at other member firms by associated persons, it also applies to securities accounts opened at non-member financial institutions such as banks and investment advisers.

question: If you want to exercise an option before the expiration date, which type of option would you need?
explanation: Only American options can be exercised before the expiration date. European options can only be exercised on the expiration date.

question: Each firm shall develop and implement a written anti-money laundering program reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's compliance with the requirements of the:
explanation: Each firm shall develop and implement a written anti-money laundering program reasonably designed to achieve and monitor the member's compliance with the requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act (31 U.S.C. 5311, et seq.), and the implementing regulations promulgated thereunder by the Department of the Treasury. Each firm's anti-money laundering program must be approved, in writing, by a member of senior management.

question: Regulation S-P limits the ability of broker-dealers, investment companies, and investment advisers to disclose __________ information about their customers with non-affiliated third parties.
explanation: Regulation S-P was put into place to protect customers from having their non-public personal information disclosed to non-affiliated third parties. It requires firms and investment companies to provide customers with a description of the type of information that will be collected, how the information will be used, and with whom it will be shared. Regulation S-P requires all firms and companies to give customers an adequate notice to opt out of sharing nonpublic personal information with third parties.

question: Sandy shorts an ABC Apr 30 call at 2.50. The stock is currently selling at 31. Which of the following is true?
choices: The intrinsic value of the option is 1
The intrinsic value of the option is 1.50
The intrinsic value of the option is 0
The intrinsic value of the option cannot be determined until the option is exercised
explanation:
For both long and short positions, call options are in-the-money when the market price is above the strike price. The intrinsic value is the amount that a stock is in the money. This is the difference between the market price and the strike price. In this case, it is $1 (31 - 30).
[Edit note - added by Claude] Feedback, last sentence: Cerifi's screen dropped the minus sign. Original: "(31 30)" Edited: "(31 - 30)"

question: A 50-year-old man has purchased a variable annuity contract. He wants payments for his life, but wants to make sure that payments are made for at least 20 years, should he die prematurely. He should choose a:
choices: joint and last survivor annuity option
systematic withdrawal plan that provides for 20 years of payments
life annuity with a 20 year period certain
explanation: A life annuity with a 20-year period certain will pay for the life of the annuitant, but if the annuitant dies early, it will pay for a minimum of 20 years regardless. These payments will be made to a designated beneficiary.

question: All of the following are types of joint accounts EXCEPT:
choices: Joint Tenants with Rights of Survivorship
explanation:
The joint account ownership options are:
Tenants in Common - each person has a divided interest with a specified ownership percentage for each party;
Joint Tenancy With Rights of Survivorship (JTWROS) - each person has an undivided interest with each owning 100% of the account; or
Tenants by Entireties - only allowed in some states, it is similar to JTWROS, however if a single tenant is sued, the assets of the joint account cannot be claimed.

Custodial accounts are not joint accounts - the minor is not authorized to trade the account nor can he or she draw checks from the account. Only the custodian can perform these actions.

question: A customer sells short 100 shares of PDQ at $47 and sells 1 PDQ Sep 50 Put @ $6. The maximum potential gain while both positions are in place is:
explanation: If the market falls, the short put is exercised and the stock must be bought at $50. Since it was already "sold" at $47, there is a loss of $3 per share ($300 total). But the customer collected $600 in premiums; so the end result is a net gain or $300. This is the maximum potential gain. Conversely, if the market rises, the short put expires, leaving a short stock position that has potentially unlimited loss.

question: Local government investment pools and 529 College Savings Plans are examples of:
explanation: A municipal fund security is a fund of securities that is issued by a state or municipality. Examples of municipal fund securities are local government investment pools and 529 College Savings Plans.

question: ABLE accounts are:
choices: used to save funds on a tax-deferred basis and may only be used to pay for medical expenses
used to save funds on a tax-deferred basis to pay for the ongoing care of disabled children below age 21
explanation:
ABLE accounts were enacted by Congress in late 2014. ABLE stands for "Achieving a Better Life Experience Act." It allows each state to set up a "municipal fund security" regulated by the MSRB that permits an account to be established to pay for the ongoing expenses of a disabled person.
One of the key features of an ABLE account is that accumulated savings do not affect that person's eligibility for other federal benefits (it used to be the case that having too much in assets would disqualify that person from other federal benefits, such as Medicaid).
The federal gift tax exclusion amount can be contributed to an ABLE account, with no tax deduction. The account grows tax-deferred, and payments to pay for qualified expenses are tax-free. Qualified expenses include medical care, transportation, housing, education, and assistive technology.
The account must be established before the disabled individual reaches age 46, and proof that the beneficiary is disabled or blind must be provided.
ABLE accounts are permitted under Section 529A of the Internal Revenue Code. Do not confuse these with 529 Plans, which are a municipal fund security to save for education expenses.

question: Employees of non-profit organizations are permitted to make salary reduction retirement plan contributions to a:
explanation: 403(b) retirement plans allow employees of non-profit institutions such as hospitals and universities to establish their own retirement plans if none is provided by the employer. The monies contributed are excluded from taxable income, and must be used to purchase "tax sheltered" annuities or mutual funds; direct stock investments are prohibited.

question: A nephew has been given a durable power of attorney over his uncle's brokerage account. Upon the death of the uncle, the power of attorney:
choices: transfers to the executor of the uncle's estate
transfers to the registered representative servicing the uncle's account
explanation: Any power of attorney, durable or non-durable, is terminated when a customer dies. The distinction between a durable and a non-durable power of attorney is that a non-durable power of attorney terminates if the grantor is mentally incapacitated whereas durable power of attorney remains in force if the grantor is mentally incapacitated.

question: An inverse ETF is most similar to taking what options position(s) on the reference index?
explanation:
An inverse ETF is unprofitable when the market rises, and profitable when the market falls. So the answer is either a Long Put or a Short Call. Since the maximum loss in a rising market is capped to the amount invested, and the gain keeps increasing as the market falls, the best choice is a Long Put, which has a maximum loss of the premium in a rising market and ever-increasing gain as the market falls.
In contrast, with a Short Call, in a rising market there is ever-increasing loss, and in a falling market, the gain is capped to the collected premium.

question: Which of the following is considered a speculative investment suitable ONLY for experienced investors who can absorb potential losses?
choices: Each of the other answer choices
explanation: Leveraged ETFs are inverse or amplified products designed for sophisticated investors. They are explicitly classified as speculative investments in the content, alongside penny stocks, crypto assets, and high-risk limited partnerships. Growth funds and high-yield bonds do come with significant risk; however, they are not considered speculative investments.

question: Which statement is TRUE when comparing a Roth IRA to a Traditional IRA?
choices: Anyone with earned income can open a Roth IRA
Anyone with investment income can open a Traditional IRA
Roth IRAs are not available to high-earning individuals
Traditional IRAs are not available to high-earning individuals
explanation:
Clients who have only investment income are not eligible to make IRA contributions.
Roth IRAs allow for the same contribution amounts as Traditional IRAs, but the contribution is never tax-deductible (which is usually the case with a Traditional IRA). Earnings build tax deferred and when distributions commence after age 59 1/2, no tax is due.
This is a very good deal. Unfortunately, the Roth IRA is not available for high-earners.

question: All of the following are types of risks that owners of variable annuities might face EXCEPT:
choices: The investor's variable annuities performs poorly due to a decline in the overall market
An investor chooses a suite of investments that do not perform well
An investor might need to withdraw the money before the surrender period is over and cannot afford the surrender charges
An investor will be unable to participate in market gains
explanation:
Variable annuities are subject to certain risks. Investors of variable annuities will have to face systematic risk. Systematic risk (also called market risk), refers to the risk that the entire market will decline, and hence the value of the securities in their variable annuity will decline with it. Funds from variable annuities are kept in accounts that are separate from the insurance company's general account, often referred to as separate accounts. Within a separate account, the investor chooses from several possible subaccounts that operate like mutual funds.
If the investments in the subaccounts perform well, the periodic payments to the annuitant will be larger, but if they perform poorly, the payments will be smaller. The investor rather than the issuer bears the investment risk. Because annuities often have long surrender periods, they should never be sold to older clients, who may need to withdraw their money before the surrender period is over. A benefit of a variable annuity is that the investor gets to participate in market gains.

question: All of the following terms apply to a variable life policy EXCEPT:
explanation:
Any "variable" product, either a variable annuity or variable life insurance, takes the premium and invests it in a designated separate account, also called a subaccount, that invests in a specified mutual fund. The performance of the mutual fund builds cash value in a variable life policy. This cash value build can be borrowed from the policy. If the cash value grows to more than the death benefit and has not been borrowed, then the policy will pay the higher cash value on death.
Variable life is "permanent insurance" - as long as the premium is paid, the policy is in effect. This contrasts with term insurance, which has a stated term, after which the policy expires and must be renegotiated. The premium amount is level - the same premium payment is paid periodically. What will vary is the cash value build and the amount of insurance coverage, based on the performance of the separate account.
In contrast, whole life is another form of permanent insurance. It invests premiums in the insurance company's general account, which is typically invested safely, mainly in bonds. The cash value builds at a fixed rate, and the coverage amount does not vary.

question: Which of the following is not true of variable annuities?
choices: They are considered to be insurance products.
They are considered to be securities.
Contributions to a variable annuity are typically made with pre-tax dollars.
The investor bears the investment risk.
explanation: Variable annuities are considered both an insurance product and a security and are subject to the regulations of both industries. The investor, rather than the issuer, bears the investment risk. Typically, a customer makes contributions into a variable annuity with after-tax dollars. Taxes on income earned in the annuity will be deferred until the money is withdrawn.

question: The Regulation T initial margin requirement for short stock positions is:
explanation: Regulation T initial margin for short stock positions is set at 50%.

question: A customer buys 100 shares of XYZ at $51 and buys 1 XYZ Jan 50 Put @ $5. The position is:
explanation: The customer is bullish due to the core long stock position and buys the put as a hedge. This makes the customer cautiously bullish since he/she has hedged the bullish stock bet with the put purchase.

question: Which of the following is true of an investor who shorts a call option?
choices: She profits when the price of the underlying security goes up
She profits when the price of the underlying security goes down
She pays a premium as part of her investment
explanation: An investor who shorts a call option profits when the price of the underlying security goes down or remains below the option's strike price. When that occurs, the option will not be exercised, and she will be able to keep the premium she received when she sold the option. The premium received is the maximum potential gain for a short options investor.

question: A representative with discretionary authority over a customer's account cannot do which of the following without the customer's prior permission?
choices: Determine a specific security to buy for a customer's account
Sell any securities from the customer's account
Decide how many shares of a specific security to buy
Withdraw money from the customer's account
explanation: Discretionary authority gives a representative third-party authority to trade in the account without prior permission from the customer. This means the representative can decide which securities to buy and sell and how many of those securities to buy and sell. However, discretionary authority does not give the representative permission to make unauthorized withdrawals from a customer's account. Only full trading authority allows a representative to make unauthorized withdrawals.

question:
Jake opens the following positions:

Long 100 GOOG at 505

Short GOOG Jun 500 call @10.

Assuming the option is assigned to Jake when it is exercised, what was Jake's profit or loss?
explanation: In this scenario, Jake has written a covered call. It is a covered call because he purchases the shares and then he writes a call on these shares. Jake purchases the shares for $50,500 (100 × $505). When he sells the call, he makes $1,000 ($10 × 100 shares). When the option is exercised, he sells the shares for $50,000. Thus, his profit is $500 (-$50,500 + $1,000 + $50,000).

question: A customer who buys a variable life policy is most susceptible to:
explanation:
The premium paid in a variable life policy is invested in a separate account that buys shares of a designated mutual fund. If the mutual fund does poorly, the account will not build cash value as quickly and the amount of coverage provided will not grow as rapidly. If the NAV of the mutual fund declines, the coverage amount can actually decline (though not below a minimum stated coverage amount). So the main risk is market risk.
Default risk is associated with investing in bonds - it is the same as credit risk. Purchasing power risk is inflation risk - and because the separate account is typically invested in equity mutual funds, where companies can raise prices if there is inflation, this risk is minimized. Finally, exchange rate risk is associated with making investments denominated in foreign currencies.

question: In a margin account the term "maintenance margin" means:
choices: The amount loaned by the broker-dealer
The rate of interest charged by the broker-dealer
The amount of equity to be maintained on a security position held or carried in an account
explanation: Maintenance margin is the minimum required collateral to maintain a margin position. Usually it is lower than the initial margin requirement. Equity in the account both initially and over time is the measuring factor in establishing and maintaining a margin account.

question: In order to recommend a variable annuity to a customer, all of the following statements are true EXCEPT:
choices: The customer must be informed, in general terms, of the material features of the product
The representative must believe that the customer would benefit from the product's features
The representative must believe that the variable product as a whole, the underlying separate accounts to which funds are allocated, and riders to the policy are suitable
The customer, representative and branch manager must all sign a statement that all required representations and determinations were completed
explanation:
In order to recommend a variable annuity to a customer, the representative must have a reasonable basis to believe that the:
- customer has been informed, in general terms, of the material features of the product;
- customer would benefit from one or more of the product's features; and
- particular variable product as a whole, the underlying separate accounts to which funds are allocated, and riders to the policy, are suitable.

The representative must sign a statement that all required representations and determinations were completed. Note that there is no customer signature here!

question: A customer owning 100 shares of stock could receive protection by:
choices: buying another 100 shares of the stock
explanation: In order to hedge a long stock position against a downside market move, the best choice is to buy a put. The long put option allows the holder to put (sell) the stock at the exercise price if the market falls - protecting the stock position from downside market risk.

question: On the same day in a margin account, a customer sells short 100 shares of ABC at $43 and buys 1 ABC Jan 45 Call @ $4. The customer will break even when:
choices: the stock falls by the amount of the premium paid
explanation:
The customer has sold short the stock at $43, hoping to profit if the price should fall. As a hedge, the customer bought the call option to buy in the stock at a price of $45 if the market should rise. This protects the short stock position from unlimited upside loss potential.
Since the customer sold the stock at $43 and paid $4 for the call option, the customer has a net sale amount of $39. To break even, the customer must buy back the stock at $39 per share, which is the sales price of $43 minus the premium of $4 paid for the call.
Note: Students are unlikely to see math calculations on hedging problems, but they must realize the short stock needs to fall by the premium paid for the customer to come out even.

question: Street name registration of common stock means the stock is registered in the name of :
explanation: Street name registration means the securities are registered in the name of the broker-dealer with the customer as the beneficial owner.

question: Which option exchange trades foreign currency options?
explanation: Trading of foreign currency options in the United States takes place only on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange. (Do not confuse this with the futures market for trading of foreign currency futures and options on futures.)

question: All of the following information is needed to open a new cash account for a customer EXCEPT:
choices: whether the customer is an officer or director of a publicly held company
whether the customer owns the stock of another publicly traded broker-dealer
whether the customer is an employee of another broker-dealer
explanation:
Country of citizenship is deemed to be an essential piece of information because the PATRIOT ACT requires that a copy of the customer's passport be obtained if an account is opened for a non-U.S. citizen and the customer must have a U.S. tax identification number.
Officers and directors of publicly held companies are restricted under federal law in their trades of that company's stock, so this information is essential.
If a customer is employed by another financial services firm, then special procedures must be followed to open the account, so this information is essential.
Whether a customer owns stock of another publicly traded broker-dealer is not essential - for example, if a customer opening an account at Merrill Lynch owns the stock of, say, Raymond James, this does not affect the opening of the account; nor how transactions are handled in the account.

question: An ABC Jan 50 Call is trading at a premium of $2 when the market price of ABC stock is $49. The time value per share is:
explanation:
The value of a premium is made up of two components: intrinsic value and time value.
premium = intrinsic value + time value
Intrinsic value is the amount per share that the holder of an option stands to gain by exercising it. Stated another way, it is the extent to which the option is in the money. This call option is out of the money because the stock price of $49 is lower than the call's strike price of $50. This means the intrinsic value is $0, and so the entire $2 premium is made up of time value.

question: As an initial transaction in a new margin account, a customer sells short 100 shares of ABC at $35. The customer must deposit:
explanation: The Regulation T requirement to sell short $3,500 of stock in a short margin account is 50% = $1,750. However, this is the initial transaction and the minimum equity to open an account is $2,000, so this amount must be deposited.

question: Regulation Best Interest applies to recommendations made to any of the following, except:
choices: A retail customer who is an associated person of the firm
A retail customer who is an accredited investor
A retail customer who is trading on margin
explanation:
Regulation Best Interest requires broker-dealers and their associated persons to act in their retail customers' best interest whenever a recommendation is made. A person is considered a retail customer for purposes of Reg BI if all of the following are true:
- The customer is a natural person or a natural person's legal representative (such as a trustee or executor). In other words, the customer is an individual rather than a legal entity such as a corporation.
- The customer receives a recommendation from a broker-dealer about any securities transaction, or any investment strategy involving securities.
- The customer uses the recommendation primarily for his personal investing (or that of his family or household). This obligation to every retail customer is not altered by the customer being an accredited investor, associated person, or margin trader.

question: Which options strategy provides the greatest profit potential in a bear market?
explanation: The purchaser of a put (long put) has the right to sell stock at a fixed price, no matter how low the market price of the stock may go. This strategy has increasing gain potential as the market falls, with the maximum gain occurring if the market falls to "0."

question: Which statement is TRUE about a cash account?
choices: All transactions must be paid for and settled the same day
All transactions must be effected in securities that are not marginable
All transactions must be paid in full on settlement
All transactions must be in DRS securities
explanation:
Regulation T of the Federal Reserve Board not only sets 50% initial margin for stock positions, it also defines which securities are marginable, defines the types of accounts in which securities transactions can be effected, and sets the time period for collection of funds when securities are purchased.
Regulation T defines both a Cash Account and a Margin Account. In a Cash Account, all purchases must be fully paid - there is no margin. In a Margin Account, the securities are pledged as collateral for a loan, and borrowing of up to 50% is allowed on an initial transaction. Regulation T applies to cash accounts where securities are fully-paid because the Federal Reserve does not want broker-dealers to tell customers something like "Pay me in full - you can pay me in 30 days" - which is the same as giving the client a 30-day loan. So Regulation T says that purchases in either a cash or margin account must be paid for "promptly" but no later than 2 business days past settlement.
Note that industry settlement rules differ from Regulation T. A "cash settlement" is same day settlement. A regular way settlement is 1 business day after trade date. Either of these can be done in a cash account or a margin account. Marginable securities can be purchased in a cash account - but they must be paid in full. Finally, DRS is the Direct Registration System - book-entry recordkeeping for securities as opposed to issuing physical certificates.

question: A prime broker provides services to:
explanation:
In a prime brokerage agreement, an institutional investor, like a hedge fund, can use different executing brokers for its trades, but all of these trades are settled by the "prime broker" who maintains custody of the positions, and most importantly, provides margin financing on these positions and arranges for stock loans on short stock positions.

By using a prime broker to consolidate all positions, the hedge fund gets lower financing costs on borrowed funds and "front of the line" status when it wishes to borrow securities to effect short sales.

question: A call option holder has the _____________ the underlying security at the option's strike price; a call option seller has the _______________ the underlying security at the option's strike price.
choices: Obligation to sell; obligation to buy
Right to sell; obligation to buy
Obligation to buy; right to sell
Right to buy; obligation to sell
explanation: A call option holder has the right to buy the underlying securities at the option's strike price, while its seller has the obligation to sell the underlying securities at the strike price when the option is exercised. Note that if a call option expires unexercised, this means the buyer did not purchase the underlying securities and the seller did not sell those same securities.

question: All of the following are true statements about trust accounts EXCEPT:
choices: a copy of the trust agreement must be obtained prior to opening the account
transactions in the account are limited to the types specified in the trust document
margin transactions are prohibited unless specific authorization to open a margin account is given in the trust document
securities that may be purchased in the account are restricted to those included in that state's "Legal List"
explanation: To open a trust account, a copy of the trust document must be obtained. The document will spell out the types of transactions that are permitted. The account must be opened as a cash account unless the document specifically permits margin transactions. Finally, there is no requirement that investments be limited to that state's "legal list" (these are lists of so-called "prudent" investments that are considered to be conservative, such as government bonds), though this can be the case if only "legal list" investments are authorized in the trust document.

question: Potential profits for a call option holder are:
choices: The same as potential profits for a call option writer
Equal to the value of the option's strike price minus its premium
Equal to the value of the option's strike price plus its premium
explanation: The potential profits for a call option holder are unlimited. This is because a call option's holder can buy the underlying securities at the option's strike price no matter how the market price of those securities has risen. Since the market price of a security can theoretically rise to infinity, this means potential profits for a long call holder are have no limit. On the other hand, the potential profit for any option writer (seller) is the premium received. A call option's breakeven point is the value of the option's strike price plus its premium. The breakeven point for a call option holder is the market value that the underlying security must rise above in order for the investor to be assured a profit on his option's investment.

question: At expiration, in-the-money S&P 500 index call options are settled by delivery of?
choices: An equal number of S&P 500 index put options
explanation: Because index options represent the collective performance of a large number of securities, settlement requires cash. It would be impossible for an investor to buy fractional shares of 500 stocks upon the expiration of an S&P 500 index option.
